description: Challenge B1 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Plausible has /ɔ/ in its first stressed syllable in General American. Possible has /ɑ/ or /ɔ/ depending on speaker and merger; this contrast can vary, so listen for the full word rather than relying on one vowel.
Endeavor begins with /ɛ/. Endower begins with /aʊ/, indoor with /ɪ/, and endure with /ɪ/.
Compass has /ʌ/ in its first syllable in General American. Campus has /æ/, composed has /oʊ/, and compost has /ɑ/.
Rendezvous begins with /ˈrɑn/ in General American. Renegade begins with /rɛ/, repertoire with /ˈrɛp/ or /ˈrɛpə/, and reliable with /rɪ/.
Pneumonia begins with /n/ because the p is silent. Pneumatic also begins /n/ but has a different vowel sequence; phenomenon begins /f/ and pseudonym begins /s/.
Gnaw begins with /n/ because the g is silent. Gnat, gnome, and gnash also begin with /n/, so the spoken vowel and ending distinguish the words.
Sixths ends with the cluster /ksθs/ in careful pronunciation. Sixth lacks the final /s/, sixes ends /ɪz/, and sickles ends /əlz/.
Heir ends with the vowel sound /ɛr/ and has a silent h. Air is a homophone of heir in General American, so this pair cannot be distinguished by sound alone; the other choices differ.
Worlds ends with /ldz/. Word ends with /rd/, works with /rks/, and worse with /rs/.
Acquaintance is spelled with -quaint- and the ending -ance. The other choices are common misspellings.
Conscience ends with -cience and is pronounced /ˈkɑnʃəns/. Conscious ends with -cious and has a different final sound; the other forms are misspellings.
Queue is spelled with five letters but pronounced like cue /kjuː/. Quay is pronounced /kiː/, while quite has /kwaɪt/.
